title: Probe: asymmetric per-token pricing (input vs output) with streaming floor and enterprise security questionnaire alignment
creator: Leah Kim
description: Run a controlled experiment to evaluate asymmetric per-token pricing where input tokens (prompt) and output tokens (generated) are charged at different rates, introduce an optional minimum monthly streaming floor for low-volume streaming customers, and surface enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) impacts for contract negotiations. The goal is to find a price surface that: (1) reduces marginal cost for prompt-heavy workloads, (2) preserves revenue for chat/streaming-heavy customers, and (3) makes enterprise procurement/security trade-offs explicit in proposals.
experiment_design: Two-factor A/B test across self-serve and sales-assisted cohorts. Factor A: per-token split variants (baseline parity, output-heavy premium, input-light discount). Factor B: streaming floor options (no floor, $50/mo floor, $200/mo floor) presented as opt-in for accounts enabling streaming endpoints. Randomize new signups and a cohort of existing paid customers who opt in via in-product banner. Track both billing and usage behaviors for 90 days.
success_metrics: median_cost_per_request reduced for prompt-heavy workloads by >=10%
sales_negotiation_time reduced for enterprise deals by >=5 days when SQ clarifications included
sq_impact_notes: We will surface a one-page SQ appendix describing how per-token rates interact with data residency and streaming telemetry. Legal will require review of language around metering and billing estimates for streaming sessions. Sales needs a templated clause for minimums and a decision tree for waiving floors in enterprise contracts.
risks: High churn risk for chat-heavy customers if output pricing increases too far. Sales pushback if minimums complicate SMB purchases. Instrumentation risk: need accurate per-token attribution for streaming partial responses.
instrumentation_todo: Add flagging for variant assignment, per-session token counters for streaming (client- and server-side), billing simulation pipeline for projected invoices, and detailed prism logs for troubleshooting mismatched metering.
implementation_notes: Billing team to implement variant hooks in metering pipeline; engineering to add streaming-floor gating in the billing config service; console UI to show projected monthly cost with floor applied. Use rollout: canary to 5% of new signups, then 20% after initial smoke tests.
